memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Follow justice and justice alone, so that you may live and possess the land the Lord your God is giving you. - Deut 16:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Follow justice and justice alone." The repetition is deliberate and forceful. God does not want a half-hearted pursuit of what is right, mixed with a little corruption here and a little favouritism there. He wants His people to chase justice single-mindedly, the way a hunter pursues his goal.

For Israel, this pursuit was tied to life in the land God was giving them. A just society would flourish; an unjust one would rot from within. God's blessing on the nation was connected to whether they upheld what was right, especially toward the weak.

We should be honest that the specific promise of the land was given to Israel under their covenant, and it is not a direct promise of property to us today. Yet God's character has not changed one bit. He still loves justice and still calls His people to pursue it wholeheartedly. Jesus reserved strong words for those who neglected justice, mercy, and faithfulness (Matt 23:23). To walk with God is to care about what He cares about. When we hunger and thirst for righteousness, we are promised satisfaction (Matt 5:6). And one day the perfectly just King will set every wrong right. Until then, we pursue justice not to earn God's favour, but because we belong to a just and holy God. What would it mean for you to pursue justice with your whole heart?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you pursuing justice wholeheartedly, or only when convenient?
2. What injustice around you troubles God's heart?
3. How can you reflect God's love of justice this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You love justice with Your whole heart. Give me the same hunger for what is right, for Your glory. Amen.
